rules.diagnosis_template: the package '{package_name}' is fractured into {n_groups} completely disconnected groups (SCPP: {scpp:.2f}).
rules.recommendation_template: This package acts as {n_groups} separate packages. Unless these are loosely coupled utilities, you MUST split this package into {n_groups} distinct packages to respect the Single Responsibility Principle.

rules.diagnosis_template: The package '{package_name}' has nearly zero structural cohesion (SCPP: {scpp:.2f}). Files behave like a random collection of scripts.
rules.recommendation_template: This implies no shared state, data, or configuration. Consider organizing these files by feature or functionality instead of grouping them arbitrarily.

rules.diagnosis_template: The package '{package_name}' contains isolated modules {{{isolated_nodes_str}}} that do not share state or data (files, globals, class attributes) with the rest of the package.
rules.recommendation_template: Verify if {{{isolated_nodes_str}}} belong here. If they are helpers, they might belong in a 'utils' package. If they are core logic, they are missing necessary data connections.

rules.diagnosis_template: The package '{package_name}' is mostly cohesive, but contains isolated modules {{{isolated_nodes_str}}}.
rules.recommendation_template: Check if {{{isolated_nodes_str}}} are standalone scripts or utilities. If so, this is acceptable. Otherwise, check for missing connections.

rules.diagnosis_template: The package '{package_name}' has excellent structural cohesion (SCPP: {scpp:.2f}). All modules share state or data resources.
rules.recommendation_template: Excellent organization. The package tightly encapsulates its data and logic.

rules.diagnosis_template: The package '{package_name}' has medium structural cohesion (SCPP: {scpp:.2f}). Modules share some resources.
rules.recommendation_template: Acceptable for a library package. For a pipeline stage, consider tightening the data dependencies or extracting shared logic.
